Q: can opencv.js really find page corners A:

I am not sure what part of the book page that you want. But here is one way in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the input

  • Convert to HSV and extract the saturation channel (note: gray has little saturation and the page is colored so that larger saturation)

  • Get the largest external contour

  • Draw that contour as white filled on a black background as a mask

  • Apply the mask to the input to blacken the background parts of the page

  • Save the resulting images

Input image:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread("bookpage.png")

# convert to HSV and get the saturation channel
hsv = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
H,S,V = cv2.split(hsv)

# threshold the saturation channel
low = (50)
high = (230)
thresh = cv2.inRange(S, low, high)

# get the largest external contour
contours = cv2.findContours(thresh, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]
big_contour = max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)

# draw that contour as white filled on a black background as a mask
mask = np.zeros_like(thresh)
cv2.drawContours(mask, [big_contour], 0, 255, -1)

# mask a copy of the input image
result = img.copy()
result[mask<255] = (0,0,0)

# save the images
cv2.imwrite("bookpage_saturation.png", S)
cv2.imwrite("bookpage_thresh.png", thresh)
cv2.imwrite("bookpage_mask.png", mask)
cv2.imwrite("bookpage_result.png", result)

# show the images
cv2.imshow("sat", S)
cv2.imshow("thresh", thresh)
cv2.imshow("mask", mask)
cv2.imshow("result", result)
cv2.waitKey(0)

Q: Using Pytube to download playlist from YouTube A:

I really understand the problem & it's solution using 'pytube', still I dare to provide some-code from myside as a solution for downloading a Youtube Playlist using 'yt_dlp'.

'''https://pypi.org/project/yt-dlp/
Install the 'yt_dlp' if you don't have it.'''
import os 
import yt_dlp

def yt_pl_downloader(yt_pl_url, yt_pl_downloads="myPlaylist"):
    """
    Following code downloads a Youtube Playlist with the URL : 'yt_pl_url' to the 'yt_pl_downloads' directory
    """
    # Ensure the save directory exists
    if not os.path.exists(yt_pl_downloads):
        os.makedirs(yt_pl_downloads)
    
    # Configure yt-dlp options
    ydl_opts = {
        #it downloads the audio & video separately and merges the output using the 'ffmpeg' library.
        
        '''install ffmpeg
           Refer 'https://ffmpeg.org/download.html'
        '''
        
        #to Limit the playlist use 'playlistend': <LIMIT>,
        'playlistend': 2,
        # Download the best available video & audio. Then, if ffmpeg is installed on your machine merging happens automatically into an mp4 file
        
        'format': 'bestvideo+bestaudio/best',
        'merge_output_format': 'mp4',
        
        # Saving the playlist to it's titled directory.
        'outtmpl': os.path.join(yt_pl_downloads, '%(playlist_title)s', '%(playlist_index)s - %(title)s.%(ext)s'),
        
        # Continue downloading even if any of the video of the playlist fails
        'ignoreerrors': True,
        
        # Ensure it treats the link as a playlist
        'noplaylist': False,
    }

    print("========Starting your download==========")
    
    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(ydl_opts) as ydl:
        try:
            ydl.download([yt_pl_url])
            print("============DONE===========")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\nAn error occurred: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    url = input("Enter your youtube playlist url: ").strip()
    
    if url:
        yt_pl_downloader(url)
    else:
        print("Enter a valid url")

The above code worked for me with Python 3.14 on Windows 11 & I used ffmpeg-9.x for merging the 'audio' & 'video' files at the end of each download.

References: https://pypi.org/project/yt-dlp/ , https://ffmpeg.org/download.html

Q: Cannot Install Node Sass with NPM A:

node-sass has been deprecated. You have to use sass.

You can uninstall the old and install the new one

npm uninstall node-sass

npm install sass

This fixes many issues also during installation

Q: Error (56): Failure when receiving data from the peer for rest API post method request using PHP A:

I have failed to send these two header in POST request 

'User-Agent:Fiddler',
"Content-length: 0",

After adding these two headers, it's working fine. Before sending your request to server, Please ask server side people about headers and parameters

Q: Android two player game to be played in internet A:

Yes, C2DM is ideally suited to this type of game. This is what I am using for my own game (http://www.chesspresso.net) which is a correspondence chess client for android.

Things to consider when using C2DM:

  • You don't send the info to the devices, you notify the devices that a move has been made. You don't use C2DM to transfer data, you use it to notify that something has changed.

  • Its available for 2.2+ Android, which is the majority of devices. But if you wanted to support older devices you'd have to consider an alternative. I am using polling for older devices.

  • You have to request for developer access, then once your app is ready you have to request production status. If you don't do this you'll hit the developer status quota very quickly once its released! They are very generous with production quota, but you have to explain what you're using it for and it also can take a few weeks to get accepted!

  • Your users will have to have a google account that is authorised, otherswise C2DM won't work. Most users will have an account associated with their device, but some don't so this means that you'll possibly want to validate for the presence of an account to notify the user.

  • Its reliable, but every now and again a device will have to wait for the message. Sometimes a few minutes. Usually its instant.

Hope that helps!

UPDATE: C2DM has now been deprecated, and replaced by Google's GCM.

Also, I strongly suggest looking at other options as tying yourself down to a Google specific API means you won't be able to support external marketplaces. For alternatives, I am currently evaluating Amazon SNS and I will also be looking at Urban Airship. There are possibly other alternatives I have not considered evaluating yet.

UPDATE: Evaluation update of non google based push notifications: Amazon SNS is just not a project for this task and Urban Airship for the vast majority of apps is too expensive. Unfortunately all the other alternatives are all very expensive also, especially if your app (like mine) relies heavily on push.
